proposal.title: Use stronger Zstd compression for published data chunks
proposal.hypothesis: Operational evidence shows Zarr metadata is 0.0% of measured output bytes and chunk payloads account for nearly all 175196006 output bytes, while the materialization path is cache-hit only. If the published data arrays keep the frozen one-sample chunk layout but explicitly use a higher Zstd compression level for data chunks, the evaluator should measure lower output_bytes without changing public array paths, coordinates, selectors, metadata validation, cache behavior, or semantic values.
proposal.expected_tradeoffs: The stronger compressor may increase materialization CPU time and could have a small effect on consumer read speed due to decompression characteristics. The public interface, chunk shape, Zarr v3 policy, and validation remain unchanged.

edits.new_text:

edits.rationale: Import the existing Zarr v3 codec implementation from an already-declared dependency so data chunk compression can be configured explicitly without adding dependencies.
Apply stronger Zstd compression only to payload-dominant data variables while preserving the existing full-field sample chunk shape and leaving coordinate encoding unchanged.

proposal.validation_plan: Rerun the evaluator and verify contract_correctness, semantic_equivalence, provenance_security, and rerun_safety remain passing. Compare output_bytes against 175196006, with secondary inspection of materialization_seconds and consumer_samples_per_second only as tradeoffs.
